[[File:FFTA2 Clan Territory.png|thumb|Clan territories in ''Tactics A2''.]]
{{Quote|Clans exist throughout Ivalice, the majority of them being quite small. Still, of those clans operating in the largest cities, many have earned a name for themselves through their accomplishments. Clan Diatroma of Bhujerba and Clan Buckaboo of Balfonheim Port are some of the more famous regional clans. Of late, a young clan in Dalmasca by the name of Clan Centurio has become a household name. Along the Phon Coast, bands of hunters fulfill the role of clans, hunting local monsters and keeping the peace.|Clans of Ivalice, [[Sage Knowledge]]}}
'''Clan''' {{J|クラン|Kuran}} is a recurring terminology in the [[Final Fantasy series|''Final Fantasy'' series]], particularly common in the world of [[Ivalice]]. It makes its first appearance in ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics Advance]]'', and has since been used to generally refer to a group of people working together for a common objective.

==Appearances==
===''[[Final Fantasy XII]]''===

{{See|Sage Knowledge 1-26#SK 22: Clans}}
Clans refer to a group of people who work together to drive away fiends and monsters known as [[Hunt (Final Fantasy XII)#Marks|marks]] from civilized areas. Entry to a clan is not publicly known; usually members of the clan would scout out potential clan members who proved their worth by defeating a mark—this happened to [[Vaan]] when [[Tomaj]] sent him to hunt the [[Rogue Tomato]].

A clan's meeting location is also made secret; clan watchmen would stand guard outside their base, permitting entry only to those with a [[Clan Primer]]. One of the famous clans in [[Rabanastre (Final Fantasy XII)|Rabanastre]] is [[Clan Centurio (Final Fantasy XII)|Clan Centurio]].

===''[[Final Fantasy XIII]]''===

The human civilization of [[Gran Pulse]] was organized in clans. Until at least the [[War of Transgression]], Gran Pulsian anthroponyms included the name of their homeland, clan name and given name, in this order.

===''[[Final Fantasy XIV]]''===

In Eorzea, clan is used to refer to subdivisions of the eight races, which players select during character creation.

===''[[Final Fantasy Tactics Advance]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy Tactics Advance clans}}
Clans make their first appearance and refers to a group of people who work together to complete missions that are posted at pubs. Anyone can be in a clan as long as they ask to be recruited. The maximum number of people in a clan cannot exceed twenty-four. Clans can earn [[Clan Titles|titles]] based on certain achievements.

Clans are led by the clan leader, who makes the decisions about who is sent out on dispatch assignments and who is entered into battle. Whenever a clan leader is not present, due to imprisonment, all clan activities stop until the return of the leader. One of the famous clans in Ivalice is [[Clan Nutsy]].

====''[[Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift]]''====
{{Main|Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift clans}}
Clans repeat the same formula used in ''Tactics Advance''. One of the famous clans known is [[Clan Gully]]. Other notable clans include [[Duelhorn]] and [[Prima Donna (clan)|Prima Donna]].
